text: Welcome to the latest episode of This is My Architecture from Mumbai. I'm Gaurav. Today
I've got Narendra Babu from Ashok Leyland who heads the analytics and emerging technologies
there. Welcome Narendra. Thanks for having me Gaurav. Tell me about Ashok Leyland. Ashok Leyland
is the second largest manufacturers of commercial vehicles in India and we produce vehicles product
range from 2.5 tons to 49 tons and we produce approximately 2 lakhs vehicles.
Lovely. Do you want to tell me about the iAnalytics platform that we are going to discuss for connected
vehicles? Sure. So Ashok Leyland predominantly used to be a customer product centric company
and now we have last 2 years we have transforming ourselves into a solution centric company for
our customer to beat into a digital marketplace. So one such product is called iAalyt and today
as we speak we have around 150,000 vehicles reporting into this platform at every 6 second
frequency and it we generate a data of 350 GB per day and we produce we process around 1
billion records per day. Wow that's a lot of data. Do you want to walk us through the real-time
architecture? Sure. So as I said vehicles are reporting at 6 second frequency and we have a third party who
collects this data and store it in Kafka in his AWS platform and we have a secure channel through which
we consume the data and we process in the live. So we have EMR cluster here and EMR in EMR we calculate
around 18 KPI's at real-time when data in motion and we store the data into S3 bucket. So the EMR uses
spark and edge bits. So can you tell us the size about of the platform? So today we have a 4 EMR clusters
with each 24 node clusters we use. And the size of the data that goes into S3 would be? Per day we generate
350 GB of data and we store for 120 days. So approximately we have around 50 terabyte of data. Oh that's
quite some data isn't it? Now how do you process the data in batch? So at every 1 hour frequency we collect the data
from S3 into another spark stream and we calculate around 99 KPI's and we store it in S3 bucket and then we
aggregate the data and we take it into a data warehouse what we use is a redshift. Right. So the structured
analytics data goes into redshift. Now I see that you've got Parquet mentioned in here as well. Can you tell me the
role of what Parquet bucket does? Correct. So S3 what we have a real-time data and it consumes a lot of space.
So what we thought is and we also store only 120 days of data here. So what we have evaluated various
options to compress this. So finally we have decided on Parquet. So we at every 1 hour frequency
we use the spark stream to take the data and we store it in Parquet. Right. And how is the data consumed on this
side? So we have various stakeholders whose needs are very different. So one such is a data analyst
when he wants data to take ad hoc reports or anything. So he consumes the data through Athena. So he takes
the data from Parquet and he generates ad hoc reports. Lovely. And the role for relational database here?
Relational database here is all the customer data, vehicle data and geospatial data generators are stored in
the RDS. Lovely. So there are different personas consuming data that has been generated. Now tell me how does machine
learning and SageMaker come into play here? So we have quite a bit of data science team here. So all their needs is they
need a real-time data as well as the aggregated data. So what they use is a SageMaker to train the model. So they consume the data from Parquet and into
SageMaker. Train the model and deploy and now create various use cases for that. Lovely. And what would the use cases be, sir?
So one of the main use cases is the fuel filterage which is predominantly used by some of my customers. And the fuel
filterage happens at the real-time they need to know. So that happens on the SageMaker platform.
That's lovely. Thanks Naren, coming down here, walking us through your architecture.
